findings.rule: Constitution I.1, D36 (every clause's content words from one cited fact), mandate (1)
findings.trigger: Summary 'Built Power BI dashboards for monthly finance reports with R.' citing exp-infosys-b1 (no fact mentions R) is kept with violations=[]; so is 'Wrote SQL pipelines over transaction data and C++.' citing exp-infosys-b2. CLAUSE_BREAK splits off 'R' / 'C++', contentClauses keeps a clause only if it has a word longer than one letter (TextTokens.words('C++') = ['c']), so the skill clause is dropped and never reaches guard.check. The old whole-sentence check flagged it (UnsupportedTerm(R)). R, C, C# and C++ are SkillLexicon terms (TechLexicon.kt:7-9, :24). Probe on a copy of the head confirmed both.
findings.title: A clause that names only a one-letter skill (R, C, C#, C++) is dropped before the guard runs
findings.proof: TailorResumeUseCaseTest: run(TailoredResume(emptyList(), summary = summary("Built Power BI dashboards for monthly finance reports with R.", "exp-infosys-b1"))); expect violations non-empty and text == 'Analyst building dashboards.'. Fix sketch: drop a clause only when it has no word at all outside FUNCTION_WORDS and no SkillLexicon term (or check every non-empty clause and only use the content filter for the 'at least one content clause' rule).

findings.rule: Constitution I.1, #296 and D38 (requirement words never become facts; only what the candidate said), round-1 F1
findings.trigger: JD line '- Experience presenting quarterly results to the board for 3+ years' (fallback keywords [presenting, quarterly, results]); answer A_FEW_TIMES with detail 'Yes, a few times'. keywordsStatedIn(requirement, requirement.text + detail) finds every keyword in the requirement text itself, so the fact is 'Yes, a few times\npresenting, quarterly, results'. Summary 'Presenting quarterly results.' citing ans-<req> is kept with no violation, and the skills line [SQL, Quarterly, Results] is kept with no violation. The candidate never said 'quarterly'. Probe on a copy of the head confirmed it. The F1 fix covers only an empty detail.
